summary: For one customer and one billing month, this procedure works out the electricity bill from the meter reading, tariff, load and taxes, saves the bill header, and skips silently if anything goes wrong.

rules.text: Each customer on the customer master is processed for the requested billing month, and the bill is only produced if a meter reading exists for that customer and month.
If no meter reading exists for the customer and month, the bill is not created for that customer and processing moves on without a message to the user.
The fixed charge and the energy charge are calculated from the tariff, the sanctioned load and the energy charge.
Fixed-charge, fuel-adjustment, electricity duty and GST amounts are calculated through the shared tax and charge routines.
The payment due date is worked out from the meter reading date.
If a payment record exists for the customer and month, its payment date is used for the late payment surcharge; if no payment record exists, the payment date is left empty.
A late payment surcharge is calculated from the energy charge, the due date and the payment date.
The television fee is 35 for tariff A1 and 60 for all other tariffs.
The television fee is not taxed and is added to the total without any tax calculation.
The total bill is the sum of energy charge, fixed charge, fuel adjustment, electricity duty, GST, television fee and late payment surcharge, rounded to a whole number.
Each bill is saved as a new bill header with the units, charges, taxes, total, due date and the date it was generated.
When the debug switch is on, a line showing the customer, month and total is printed for each bill.
Any other error stops the processing for the whole run silently: the error is caught and ignored, so no bill or error is reported and the batch continues.
